open_points.subject: _registry_url
open_points.text: Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the transport_error member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw KeyError, ValueError, or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the variable is absent or empty; its value is not a usable http or https base URL; its value carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.
open_points.other_text: - RegistryFailureKind enum members: ARCHIVED='archived', HTTP_ERROR='http_error', IDENTITY_MISMATCH='identity_mismatch', INVALID_UUID='invalid_uuid', NOT_FOUND='not_found', SCHEMA_MISMATCH='schema_mismatch', TIMEOUT='timeout', TRANSPORT_ERROR='transport_error'
open_points.question: Must the note name the TRANSPORT_ERROR member, or does “transport_error member” mean the value of the uppercase TRANSPORT_ERROR member?

open_points.subject: _translate_registry_failure
open_points.text: - _translate_registry_failure: [BEHAVIOR] MUST translate each closed failure into its member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, so an invalid identifier gives its invalid_uuid member, an unknown project its not_found member, an inactive project its archived member, a timeout its timeout member, a transport failure its transport_error member, a non-success HTTP status its http_error member, an invalid body its schema_mismatch member and a response for another project its identity_mismatch member, and MUST NOT fall back to cached, client-supplied, or fabricated context.

open_points.question: Must the note use the declared uppercase member names INVALID_UUID, NOT_FOUND, ARCHIVED, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT_ERROR, HTTP_ERROR, SCHEMA_MISMATCH, and IDENTITY_MISMATCH, or are its lowercase terms intended to denote enum values rather than members?
